Step 1: Understand what Oscar Wilde was convicted of. In 1895, Oscar Wilde was prosecuted and convicted under Section 11 of the UK's Criminal Law Amendment Act 1885 for "gross indecency" with other men. This law criminalized all homosexual acts between men, regardless of consent or whether they occurred in private.

Step 2: Examine current US law regarding same-sex relations. In the United States, the legal landscape regarding consenting adults in private has fundamentally changed. In the landmark 2003 Supreme Court case *Lawrence v. Texas*, the Court ruled that laws criminalizing private, consensual homosexual conduct are unconstitutional, violating the Due Process Clause of the Fourteenth Amendment. 

Step 3: Compare Wilde's prosecution to modern US legal standards. Under contemporary US law, the private, consensual acts for which Wilde was prosecuted are constitutionally protected and cannot be criminalized by the government. Prosecuting someone for consensual same-sex relations today would be a direct violation of fundamental constitutional rights to privacy and liberty.

Step 4: Conclude whether his treatment would be considered fair. Because the very basis of his criminal conviction is unconstitutional and considered a severe violation of human and civil rights under current US law, his treatment would not be considered fair today.
